record.text: The UI Designer will design the LCD screen menu for all functions.
Teletext functionality will not be included in the remote because it is outdated.
The target user group will be users below forty.
Ownership and accountability of decisions are unclear due to delegation phrases with no explicit owner.
The corporate identity should be clear in the remote design, with the corporate logo placed on the top-left, aligned with the screen.
The product will be designed to control only one device.

Place the screen on the top of the remote, adopt the look-and-feel of the left example, and integrate speech recognition with basic functions placed on the device and advanced features hidden behind a screen menu.
Include an equaliser with treble and bass, a mono/stereo option for the sound output, and pitch control.
The UI designer will make a list of the functions to be included on the screen.
The UI designer will create maps with all the data we have gathered.
The Project Manager will write the minutes.

gold.text: Marketing presented reported user research that existing remotes are unattractive, often lost, time-consuming to learn and associated with RSI concerns.
Marketing reported that power, channel and volume controls are frequently used, while audio and screen settings are used less often but may still be needed.
The team emphasized usability and an attractive look and feel, while recognizing a tradeoff between fashionable form and functionality.
Management's new requirements were television-only operation, no teletext, a target market below 40 and recognizable corporate identity; the group later selected an approximate 16-40 target range.
The user interface designer contrasted a complex remote with a simple one and recommended combining their best features.
The team chose to incorporate an LCD and speech recognition for the younger target market.
The industrial designer described the signal path in a remote, but said that late instructions had prevented him from completing an informed design presentation.
The team discussed the required functions and sketched a tentative layout, including basic controls, a screen, microphone and corporate logo.
They chose direct buttons for basic functions and an LCD menu for less-used advanced settings.
They discussed shared channel/volume navigation controls and separate menu, confirm and back controls, with LEDs indicating active buttons.
The project manager will write and place the meeting minutes in the project folder.
The user interface designer will develop the remote layout and a user-friendly LCD menu, including navigation and button usage.
The industrial designer will define the functional aspects and the list of functions to include in the LCD menu, coordinating with the user interface designer.
Include an LCD screen and speech recognition.
Access less-used advanced functions, including audio settings, screen settings and channel programming, through the LCD menu; retain direct controls for basic functions.
Target approximately ages 16-40, following management's below-40 direction and the age range covered by the research.
Exclude teletext under the new management requirements.
Restrict the remote to television control, superseding the provisional television-and-video scope.
Include the corporate logo and corporate colours in the remote's design.
Place the LCD at the top and favor a top-position microphone, leaving detailed placement to the designer.
Use LEDs under the buttons to show which controls are active in the current mode.
Computer/display problems disrupted preparation and presentation; the screen-size problem was adjusted and the presentation was brought back online during the meeting.
The industrial designer received key instructions too late to incorporate them fully, leaving the presentation and design incomplete.

The industrial and user interface designers initially disputed their responsibilities. They settled on industrial design defining functions and user interface design arranging the layout and menu, with coordination between them.
The project manager will reorganize the shared project information into clearer folders.
